facts.title: Labelforge annotation platform accessed with stolen employee credential
facts.known: Someone logged into Labelforge's annotation platform using a stolen employee credential. Labelforge's security team spotted the login at 6:00 AM on Nov 2 and emailed us about it at 3:00 PM the same day.
facts.not_yet_known: What data was viewed or downloaded.

rows.why: Labelforge, acting as ExampleCo's subcontractor, held two AHS limited data sets, and this BAA treats limited data sets as PHI for every purpose. Someone logged into Labelforge's platform with a stolen credential, which is a successful unauthorized access and therefore a reportable Security Incident under Section 4.2. Whether it is also a Breach depends on what was viewed or downloaded, and that is not yet known.

evidence.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
evidence.point: Both batches are limited data sets, so they are PHI for reporting purposes.

evidence.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
evidence.point: Only safe-harbor data is excluded. These batches kept service dates and ZIP codes, so they are not safe harbor.

evidence.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
evidence.point: The definition reaches incidents at Subcontractors that maintain ePHI for AHS.

evidence.quote: "Subcontractor" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
evidence.point: Labelforge maintains AHS PHI on ExampleCo's behalf, so it is a Subcontractor.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
evidence.point: Report is owed. The clock runs from ExampleCo's awareness.

evidence.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
evidence.point: The standing-notice carve-out does not apply. This login succeeded and was not blocked.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
evidence.point: A separate Breach report applies if the risk assessment finds a Breach.

evidence.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
evidence.point: Viewing or downloading by the intruder would be an impermissible disclosure.

rows.clock_reason: Section 4.2 runs from when 'Business Associate becomes aware' of the Security Incident, which was when Labelforge emailed ExampleCo at 3:00 PM on Nov 2, 2026, not when Labelforge spotted the login.

also_do.quote: in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery
also_do.point: Have Labelforge disable the stolen credential and preserve its access and download logs now. The Breach risk assessment and any later Breach report depend on that evidence.

also_do.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
also_do.point: Send the written Security Incident report to privacy-office@ahs.example with a copy to iso@ahs.example within the 4.2 window, after counsel reviews it.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
also_do.point: Run the HIPAA breach risk assessment now. Treat Discovery as possibly 6:00 AM Nov 2, when Labelforge spotted the login.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
also_do.point: Once Labelforge confirms whether AHS batches were viewed or downloaded, file the 4.3 report within 10 days of learning it.

also_do.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
also_do.point: Gather the 4.5 elements: affected individuals, which needs AHS help because names were removed; PHI involved; Breach and Discovery dates; mitigation steps.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
also_do.point: Send follow-up updates to the same addresses as facts develop. The contract sets no update cadence, so agree one with AHS.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
also_do.point: Pull Labelforge's written subcontractor BAA and confirm it carries the reporting, US-only and HITRUST terms.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
also_do.point: Keep a complete incident record, including timeline, communications and the risk assessment, in case HHS reviews it.

also_do.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
also_do.point: If ExampleCo ends or narrows its use of Labelforge, require return or destruction of both batches with certification. Do this only after evidence is preserved.

also_do.quote: agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA
also_do.point: Any replacement labeling vendor must sign a written flow-down agreement before receiving AHS PHI, including the US-only (3.2) and HITRUST (3.3) terms.

also_do.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
also_do.point: Leave notice to individuals, regulators and media to AHS. Track the reimbursable costs if a Breach is confirmed.

legal_flags.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2)
legal_flags.point: The batch records list 'limited_data_set' as their de-identification method. Check whether ExampleCo handled these batches as de-identified, outside the BAA, when it sent them to Labelforge.

legal_flags.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
legal_flags.point: Service dates and ZIP codes were sent to a labeling vendor for reviewer-feedback work. Assess whether that was the minimum necessary.

legal_flags.quote: in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery
legal_flags.point: Discovery under HIPAA may be imputed from Labelforge's 6:00 AM detection if Labelforge is ExampleCo's agent. The contract also does not say how 4.1 and 4.2 interact.

legal_flags.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
legal_flags.point: ExampleCo has potential cost exposure for a Breach caused by its Subcontractor. Consider recovery from Labelforge.

open_questions: Were either of the AHS batches (LF-2026-0602, LF-2026-0915) viewed or downloaded, and could the stolen credential reach them?
When did the unauthorized access begin, and how long did it last?
Does the HIPAA risk assessment show a low probability of compromise, or is this a Breach of Unsecured PHI under 4.1?
Did Labelforge sign a written subcontractor BAA under 5.1, and does it include reporting deadlines, US-only handling and HITRUST terms?
Was the login made from outside the United States, and does Labelforge store or access the data only in the US (3.2)?
Does Labelforge's annotation platform hold HITRUST r2 certification (3.3)?
Is Labelforge ExampleCo's agent under federal agency law, which would set Discovery at 6:00 AM Nov 2?
Can AHS identify affected individuals from record context, since names and record numbers were removed?
Was any other AHS data on the platform beyond the two batches listed?
Will ExampleCo continue, suspend or end the Labelforge relationship?

notice_draft.subject: BAA AHS-BAA-2025-0211: Security Incident report under Section 4.2 (subcontractor Labelforge)
notice_draft.body:
To the Amazing Health System Privacy Office (copy: Information Security Office):

Under Section 4.2 of Business Associate Agreement AHS-BAA-2025-0211, ExampleCo, Inc. reports a Security Incident at its subcontractor, Labelforge. Labelforge provides an annotation platform.

What we know:
- Someone logged into Labelforge's annotation platform using a stolen Labelforge employee credential.
- Labelforge's security team spotted the login at 6:00 AM ET on November 2, 2026.
- Labelforge notified ExampleCo by email at 3:00 PM ET the same day.

EHS data held on the platform at the time:
- Two batches of reviewer feedback on claims-triage agent outputs, from ExampleCo's AI agent builder.
- Both are limited data sets under 45 C.F.R. 164.514(e). Names and record numbers were removed. Service dates and ZIP codes were kept.
- Batch LF-2026-0602 (sent June 2, 2026): 2,700 records.
- Batch LF-2026-0915 (sent September 15, 2026): 3,100 records.
- Under Section 2.4 of the BAA, this data is PHI.

What is not yet known:
- Whether any AHS data was viewed or downloaded.
- When the unauthorized access began. The time above is when the login was spotted.
- Whether this is a Breach of Unsecured PHI. That determination is pending.
- Which individuals, if any, are affected.

Steps taken: [TO BE COMPLETED BY EXAMPLECO: describe only steps confirmed to have been taken]

If we determine that a Breach or an impermissible use or disclosure occurred, we will report it under Sections 4.1 and 4.3. That report will include the information required by Section 4.5 to the extent known. We will send updates as we learn more.

Contact: [NAME, TITLE, EMAIL, PHONE]

ExampleCo, Inc.
